referenced_urls.title: Tampered ML: Evaluating LLM Judgment of Machine Learning Research

relevance: Measures whether models can vet research methodology — key for automated research agents.

media.description: Screenshot of the Tampered ML paper abstract: 1,858 item-pairs of ML experiment proposals vs minimally edited flawed counterfactuals, testing whether models can spot methodological flaws to help automate alignment research.
media.ocr_text: One approach to accelerating progress on AI alignment is to automate parts of alignment research itself. Doing so requires systems that can perform reliably on hard-to-supervise research tasks, including identifying flaws in research proposals and evaluating whether a proposed experiment supports its intended claim. To evaluate this capability, we introduce Tampered ML, a benchmark of 1,858 item-pairs, each consisting of an experiment proposal reconstructed from a published machine learning paper and a minimally edited counterfactual that introduces a targeted methodological flaw. Models must identify the more methodologically sound proposal in both presentation orders. A human validation study on a stratified sample estimates that 86% of items are valid (95% CI: 81-91%).
